title: One-time 1.17.2 strategy review
standard: Authored judgments from 1.17.2 kits (Pred.gg version 169), the official 1.17.2 changes, the 1.17.2 build pass plans and role economy, weighed against Pred.gg Gold+ 1.17.2 role results collected 17 October 2026 (about four days since the 13 October release, roughly 9,000 games per role; Bronze+ contains the same games). Each grade was compared with its previous reference sample (the 1.17 review or the 1.17 line). A grade moved at most one step, and only with a kit or patch reason and evidence pointing the same way, or under the drop rule: one step down without a kit reason when a 95% interval over at least 500 games excludes the previous reference rate. A high rate alone never raises a grade, and a sample under 100 games is not graded on alone; the two roles with fewer than 100 Gold+ 1.17.2 games keep their previous sample. Grades are not calculated win probabilities, source-provided tiers, or proven optimal picks. A 3 percentage-point change from the listed sample with at least 500 current games flags the grade for review; that trigger is not a significance test. Refreshing data does not rewrite this review.

build_adaptations.reason: Rapture supplies health, attack speed and close-range, health-based on-hit damage; Double Pain explicitly applies on-hit twice. Trade away Mutilator's power, haste, higher omnivamp and ability-trigger pattern. Kiting still defeats the plan. 1.17.2 fixed Mutilator so it applies when an area ability damages several enemies, which raises the cost of giving it up in grouped fights.
build_adaptations.why_verdict: The swap still holds, but the 1.17.2 Mutilator bugfix makes the replaced item stronger on area hits such as Double Pain's cleave, so the trade-off now says so. Double Pain's higher mana cost and base power cut do not affect the swap.

You give up Mutilator's power, haste, larger omnivamp and ability-triggered hits. sequence.note: The blade tether limits movement for 1.45s but does not establish a stun. Recalling the blade early ends the tether.
sequence.why_verdict: 1.17.2 raised the tether from 1.3s to 1.45s, so the note's duration is updated. A boundary that limits movement is still a boundary, not a stun or a hold, so boundary, direct, boundary and none still fit.

capability.reason: Combat Veteran adds passive experience and 2.5% movement speed. It changes levelling pace, not Lt. Belica's control or damage tools.
capability.why_verdict: 1.17.2 cut the augment's movement speed from 3% to 2.5% and its passive experience to 0.1-2; the reason quoted 3%, so it now says 2.5%. Innovation's haste per maxed ability (10 to 8) does not affect the capability. No tag change.

capability.reason: Bramble Patch has 30% more range. The augment does not change the slow or the allied movement speed; it extends where they can be placed.
capability.why_verdict: 1.17.2 cut the patch's allied movement speed from 15% to 12%. The old wording 'are unchanged' could read as a patch claim, so it now says the augment does not change them. No tag change.

compositions.name: Containment into Black Hole
compositions.why_verdict: Picks kept. Zarus moved S to A in jungle, but his job here is containment, which is intact: Coliseum still leaps at an enemy hero and summons the arena for 4s. 1.17.2 lowered Coliseum's damage (200/325/450 to 180/305/430, bonus physical scaling 100% to 90%) and his base physical power, so the weakness now says the kill must come from Black Hole. Gideon had no 1.17.2 change; the 2.75s Black Hole line is still exact. The Ground sentence is dated 'since 1.17' and names Valmont's bind as his 1.17.2 Arterial Grip text does ('grounded', broken by crowd control on Valmont), so a Zarus Barricade stun still breaks it.

compositions.name: Direct catch, compact burst
compositions.why_verdict: Picks kept. Steel's Shield Bash and Shield Slam are unchanged. Lt. Belica moved S to A in midlane: 1.17.2 lowered Seismic Assault damage and raised its cooldown (16-12 to 17-13), lowered Void Bomb damage and cut Innovation's haste per maxed ability (10 to 8). The plan's sequence (stun, then Seismic Assault and Void Bomb, not both controls at once) holds and matters more with a longer cooldown, so the weakness now states the trims. Steel's jungle sample is still small (141 Gold+ 1.17.2 games), and the official 1.17 Heavy Metal spell-shield rule is unchanged.

compositions.name: Second-wave dive
compositions.why_verdict: Retained. Neither Serath nor Mourn had a 1.17.2 hero change. Abduct still pulls the first enemy hit and slows it 90%, Heaven's Fury still teleports on the final strike, and the visage still grants a free Heresy and a 65% basic-cooldown cut only after a takedown. Serath stays A; the 1.17.2 Weald and Wind-Rider trims touch her loadout, not this sequence.

compositions.name: Buy time for Sparrow
compositions.why_verdict: Retained. Muriel and Sparrow had no 1.17.2 hero change and keep S. Consecrated Ground and Alacrity still grant attack speed, healing, a shield and movement speed, and Heightened Senses is still a stealth reposition, so Sparrow still needs other roles for the opening and a durable body. Weald and Wind-Rider trims are small loadout changes.

compositions.name: Protect the channel
compositions.why_verdict: Retained. The text quotes no Coliseum or Reversal number. Reversal of Fortune's 1.17.2 text still gives 30% damage reduction and a shield while Muriel flies to any allied hero, Gideon's 2.75s line is exact, and the Torn Space Ground rule is unchanged. Zarus's Coliseum damage cut and his move to A do not affect setting the target; Muriel stays S.

compositions.name: Catch, silence, convert
compositions.why_verdict: Retained. Steel is unchanged. Belica's 1.17.2 trims lower her burst but keep the layered stun-then-burst sequence. Drongo lost 1 base physical power and some health and armor, but Gag Grenade's silence, Rad Rounds and Shrapnel Cannon's in-air push-back are unchanged, and he stays S. The weakness already asks another role for protection.

compositions.name: Grouped sustain and cleanup
compositions.why_verdict: Picks kept. Aurora's 1.17.2 change is a bug fix: Glacial Charge's ice now grants her and her allies its movement speed while on it, which serves 'move together', so the plan names it. Narbash had no 1.17.2 change and Legion's area plan is unchanged; Legion stays A. Cryoseism's 1.5s delay is unchanged, so 'partly delayed' still holds.

compositions.name: Peel before damage
compositions.why_verdict: Retained. Steel, Muriel and Sparrow had no 1.17.2 hero change. Steel's stuns and Force Shield still let him take first contact and keep a control for the diver; Muriel still keeps Sparrow firing. None of the three is a magical damage plan, so the weakness stands.

compositions.name: Controlled front-to-back
compositions.why_verdict: Picks kept. Greystone (A) lost some of Assault The Gates' cooldown refund on a hero hit (35% to 30%), and the refund now occurs only on a hero or camp leader hit; the weakness adds this because the plan uses him to pressure space. Stone Forged Soul is unchanged (2.5s stasis heal with a proximity slow). Steel, Gideon, Sparrow and Mourn had no 1.17.2 change; the 2.75s line is exact.

compositions.name: Compact catch with protection
compositions.why_verdict: Retained. Zarus and Belica moved to A on 1.17.2 damage and cooldown trims, but the plan uses them only to identify a single target, which their kits still do. Drongo's silence and in-air blast are unchanged, Muriel still protects the damage window, and Akeron (B since 3 Oct) had no 1.17.2 change. The overcommit warning stands.

compositions.name: Prepared objective control
compositions.why_verdict: Picks kept. The Fey stays S in midlane; 1.17.2 trimmed Harvest Nettles' damage and Bramble Patch's ally movement speed (15% to 12%), but Bramble Patch and the delayed Fly Trap pull still need enemies to stay nearby, as the weakness says. Aurora's Glacial Charge fix now gives allies on the ice its movement speed, which helps 'arrive first', so the plan names it. Greystone's refund trim does not affect occupying the second angle; Legion and Narbash are unchanged.

compositions.name: Protected second entry
compositions.why_verdict: Retained. Akeron, Serath, Eden and Steel had no 1.17.2 hero change; Steel support moved S to A under the drop rule, without a kit change, and his Shield Bash, Shield Slam and Force Shield still let him establish contact and save a control. Belica's trims do not stop her confirming a target. The execution warning stands.

pools_why: Jungle (reordered): Khaimera moves to first as the new S jungler (1.17.2 Ambush scaling 70% to 80% and a flat 40% slow; 55.7% over 2,501 Gold+ games, interval excluding his 51.6% reference upward) and Aurora stays S second. Zarus moves from first to third after his S to A move (Coliseum and base power cut; interval excludes his reference); he stays for the containment job the compositions use. Serath, Steel and Rampage keep their A grades and order. Sevarog (B to A, 308 games) is not added: the pool already covers his frontline job and his sample is small. Midlane (changed): The Fey leads as the only S midlaner. Lt. Belica moves to second after her S to A move; she stays for the compact catch the compositions use. Gideon (A) stays third. Renna is added fourth after her B to A move (stronger Mortal Coil and a passive-stacking fix; 51.9% over 2,236, interval excludes her 49.0% reference), ahead of Argus, whose A was retained without a kit change. Offlane (changed): Greystone leads; his A was retained (51.0% over 2,052) and no offlaner holds S. Shinbi (A) stays second. Kwang is added third after his B to A move (tether 1.3s to 1.45s, Surge and Fury damage up; 50.9% over 1,151, interval excludes his 47.3% reference). Grux moves from first to fourth after his A to B move (base power and Double Pain cost; 49.2% over 1,546). Akeron (B) stays last for sustain and frontline. Support (reordered): the three S supports lead, Mourn, Muriel and Narbash; Steel moves from second to last after his S to A drop-rule move (no kit change; 49.4% over 2,381, interval excludes his 51.5% reference). He stays for the direct opening. Carry (unchanged): Drongo, Sparrow and Eden keep S and Legion keeps A. TwinBlast (B to A) is not added because his move rests on the buffs, not the sample; Revenant fell to B and was not in the pool. Every pooled hero has a reviewed grade and plan in that role, and no pool leads with a hero this review moved down.
